source.source: NASA PDS ChemCam preflight laboratory calibration spectra
source.instrument: ChemCam flight model, LANL cleanroom preflight Test 6
source.license_evidence: NASA dataset page explicitly declares us-pd and links USA.gov public-domain label 1.0; applies to the matching DATA_SET_ID in the downloaded PDS label. This is not inferred from archive publicity.

wavelength_medium_evidence.locator: Wiens et al. 2013, wavelength calibration discussion: Ti baseline channel-to-wavelength map
wavelength_medium_evidence.basis: The paper states that all spectra are adjusted to its Ti baseline wavelength-channel map. The official CALINFO identifies the preflight cleanroom calibration with this paper and Test 6.

composition_evidence.interpretation: Ground calibration standard compositions, not Mars MOC predictions. The PDS calibration field descriptions reuse the word Predicted, but CALINFO and the primary Table 3 identify standards and their reference compositions. FeOT converts the table total Fe2O3 convention; only positive presence is evaluated.

source.preprocessing_by_provider: dark subtraction, denoising, continuum removal, wavelength calibration and instrument response correction

reference_metadata.cleaning_rules: observed preferred within transition; Ritz fallback; exact duplicates removed; raw fields preserved
reference_metadata.notice: NIST atomic lines are reference data, not measured mixture spectra. Relative intensities from different elements are not concentration calibration.

limitations: Only positive-reference recall is identifiable; no precision/F1 claim.
H and He are unlabelled. Four elements evaluated where composition is positive.
One external acquisition campaign; no real transfer fitting occurred.
Neutral Gaussian training omits ionic/molecular plasma physics and interferents.
Observation windows fixed from documentation before prediction.
Research models use an observation mask; do not replace the general API models.
